claim: Piezo 1 and 2 are mechanosensitive ion channels
source: The mechanosensitive ion channels Piezo 1 and 2 induce a curved protein-membrane nanodome that flattens with increasing membrane tension γ.
evidence: Supported by citation to Coste et al., 2010; Coste et al., 2012 in the Introduction

claim: Piezo proteins induce a curved protein-membrane nanodome
source: The mechanosensitive ion channels Piezo 1 and 2 induce a curved protein-membrane nanodome that flattens with increasing membrane tension γ.
evidence: Supported by simulation data and citations to experimental work

claim: The Piezo protein-membrane nanodome flattens with increasing membrane tension
source: The mechanosensitive ion channels Piezo 1 and 2 induce a curved protein-membrane nanodome that flattens with increasing membrane tension γ.
evidence: Supported by simulation data showing tension-dependent flattening

claim: The tension-induced flattening of the nanodome is associated with Piezo activation
source: The tension-induced flattening of the nanodome is associated with Piezo activation and driven by the energy γΔA where ΔA is the excess area of the curved nanodome relative to its planar projected area.
evidence: Based on established mechanistic understanding from literature

claim: The tension-induced flattening is driven by the energy γΔA
source: The tension-induced flattening of the nanodome is associated with Piezo activation and driven by the energy γΔA where ΔA is the excess area of the curved nanodome relative to its planar projected area.
evidence: Based on theoretical framework from Guo and MacKinnon, 2017

claim: The excess area ΔA for the Piezo protein-membrane nanodome is about 40 nm² in tensionless membranes
source: Based on extensive coarse-grained and atomistic simulations of membrane-embedded Piezo 1 and 2 proteins, we report here an excess area ΔA for the Piezo protein-membrane nanodome of about 40 nm2 in tensionless membranes
evidence: Directly measured from simulation data

claim: Half-maximal reduction of ΔA occurs at tension values of about 3–4 mN/m
source: we report here an excess area ΔA for the Piezo protein-membrane nanodome of about 40 nm2 in tensionless membranes, and a half-maximal reduction of ΔA at tension values of about 3–4 mN/m
evidence: Calculated from simulation data

claim: The half-maximal reduction tension of 3–4 mN/m is within the range of experimentally determined values for the half-maximal activation of Piezo 1
source: a half-maximal reduction of ΔA at tension values of about 3–4 mN/m, which is within the range of experimentally determined values for the half-maximal activation of Piezo 1.
evidence: Comparison with experimental data from Lewis and Grandl, 2015; Cox et al., 2016

claim: Membrane-embedded Piezo proteins adopt conformations that are significantly less curved than the protein conformation in detergent micelles of cryo-EM structures
source: In line with recent experimental investigations of Piezo proteins in cell membranes and membrane vesicles, the membrane-embedded Piezo proteins adopt conformations in our simulations that are significantly less curved than the protein conformation in the detergent micelles of cryo-EM structures.
evidence: Supported by simulation data and comparison with experimental observations

claim: Piezo proteins resist flattening with a force constant of about 60 pN/nm
source: According to this model, the Piezo proteins resist flattening with a force constant of about 60 pN/nm.
evidence: Derived from elasticity analysis of simulation data

claim: Piezo 1 and 2 mediate numerous physiological processes in mammals, including touch sensation and blood pressure control
source: The transmembrane (TM) proteins Piezo 1 and 2 are mechanosensitive ion channels (Coste et al., 2010; Coste et al., 2012) that mediate numerous physiological processes in mammals, including touch sensation and blood pressure control (Wu, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wu, 2017

claim: Cryo-EM structures of Piezo 1 revealed three identical monomeric arms with 38 TM helices
source: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of Piezo 1 (Guo and MacKinnon, 2017; Saotome et al., 2018; Zhao et al., 2018) and Piezo 2 (Wang et al., 2019) in detergent micelles revealed three identical monomeric arms with 38 TM helices that spiral out from the central ion channel
evidence: Supported by citations to cryo-EM structure papers

claim: The central ion channel is lined by the innermost TM helices of the arms
source: revealed three identical monomeric arms with 38 TM helices that spiral out from the central ion channel, which is lined by the innermost TM helices of the arms.
evidence: Supported by citations to cryo-EM structures

claim: The TM domains of the helices in the three arms do not lie in a plane
source: The TM domains of the helices in the three arms do not lie in a plane, which led to the suggestions that the Piezo protein curves the cell membrane into a nanodome
evidence: Observation from cryo-EM structures

claim: Cryo-electron tomography images of reconstituted membrane vesicles with embedded Piezo 1 proteins show that the proteins induce membrane curvature
source: Cryo-electron tomography images of reconstituted membrane vesicles with embedded Piezo 1 proteins indeed show that the proteins induce membrane curvature (Guo and MacKinnon, 2017)
evidence: Supported by citation to experimental work

claim: The induced curvature in membrane vesicles is on average about four times smaller than the curvature of the proteins in detergent micelles
source: but elastic modeling of vesicle shapes with varying diameters indicates that this induced curvature is on average about four times smaller than the curvature of the proteins in the detergent micelles of the high-resolution cryo-EM structures (Haselwandter et al., 2022a; Haselwandter et al., 2022b).
evidence: Supported by citations to elastic modeling studies

claim: High-resolution fluorescence imaging of Piezo 1 in its native cell membrane environment confirms an expansion in the inactivated state from flattening of the arms compared to structural models in detergent micelles
source: High-resolution fluorescence imaging of Piezo 1 in its native cell membrane environment confirms an expansion in the inactivated state from flattening of the arms compared to structural models in detergent micelles and indicates further flattening upon activation (Mulhall et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation to experimental work

claim: A cryo-EM structure of flattened Piezo 1 with widened ion channel has been obtained by embedding Piezo 1 proteins in small membrane vesicles with a diameter of 20 nm in an outside-out orientation
source: A cryo-EM structure of flattened Piezo 1 with widened ion channel has been obtained by embedding Piezo 1 proteins in small membrane vesicles with a diameter of 20 nm in an outside-out orientation in which the vesicle curvature opposes the intrinsic Piezo curvature (Yang et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to experimental work

claim: In patch-clamp experiments, an opening of the ion channel induced by membrane tension has been observed for Piezo 1, but not for Piezo 2
source: In patch-clamp experiments with Piezo 1 and Piezo 2, an opening of the ion channel induced by membrane tension has been observed for Piezo 1, but not for Piezo 2, which appears to indicate that Piezo 2 activation requires other factors of its cellular context that are not present in the experiments, besides membrane tension (Moroni et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to experimental work

claim: Piezo 2 activation requires other factors of its cellular context besides membrane tension
source: which appears to indicate that Piezo 2 activation requires other factors of its cellular context that are not present in the experiments, besides membrane tension (Moroni et al., 2018).
evidence: Inference from experimental observations

claim: The relaxed simulation structure of Piezo 2 in tensionless membranes is significantly flattened compared to the cryo-EM structure of the Piezo 2 trimer in detergent micelles
source: We find that the relaxed simulation structure of Piezo 2 in tensionless membranes is significantly flattened compared to the cryo-EM structure of the Piezo 2 trimer in detergent micelles (see Figure 1).
evidence: Directly observed in simulation data and shown in Figure 1

claim: The nanodome with constrained cryo-EM structure has a height of 10 nm
source: From the simulation trajectories in which the protein structure is constrained to the cryo-EM structure of Piezo 2 in detergent micelles, we obtain a nanodome midplane shape with a height of 10 nm
evidence: Measured from simulation data with constrained protein structure

claim: The nanodome with relaxed Piezo 2 protein has a height of about 4 nm
source: we obtain a nanodome midplane shape with a height of 10 nm, which is significantly larger than the height of about 4 nm for the nanodome shape with the relaxed Piezo 2 protein.
evidence: Measured from simulation data with relaxed protein structure

claim: The maximal mean curvature of the nanodome with constrained protein structure is about two times larger than the maximal mean curvature of the nanodome with the relaxed protein
source: In these mean curvature profiles, the maximal mean curvature of the nanodome with constrained protein structure is about two times larger than the maximal mean curvature of the nanodome with the relaxed protein.
evidence: Calculated from simulation data shown in Figure 1c

claim: The mean curvature of the nanodome with the relaxed Piezo 2 protein drops to 0 for radial distances larger than about 17 nm from the channel center
source: The mean curvature of the nanodome with the relaxed Piezo 2 protein drops to 0 for radial distances larger than about 17 nm from the channel center, which indicates a catenoidal shape of the non-planar surrounding membrane
evidence: Calculated from simulation data

claim: The average height of the nanodome decreases to 1.6 nm at membrane tension of 10.8 mN/m
source: and to 1.6 nm and 0.9 nm at the largest tensions of 10.8 mN/m and 20.8 nM/m (see radial nanodome profiles in Figure 2d).
evidence: Measured from coarse-grained simulation data

claim: The average height of the nanodome decreases to 0.9 nm at membrane tension of 20.8 mN/m
source: and to 1.6 nm and 0.9 nm at the largest tensions of 10.8 mN/m and 20.8 nM/m (see radial nanodome profiles in Figure 2d).
evidence: Measured from coarse-grained simulation data

claim: In atomistic simulations of membrane-embedded Piezo 2, a comparable tension-induced flattening of the Piezo 2 protein-membrane nanodome is observed
source: In atomistic simulations of membrane-embedded Piezo 2, we observe a comparable tension-induced flattening of the Piezo 2 protein-membrane nanodome, and a comparable height of the nanodome in tensionless membranes, which corroborates our coarse-grained simulation results (see Figure 3).
evidence: Observed in atomistic simulation data

claim: The force modeling is consistent with the Piezo cryo-EM structure in detergent micelles as force-free conformation of the protein
source: Our force modeling thus is consistent with the Piezo cryo-EM structure in detergent micelles as force-free conformation of the protein.
evidence: Inference from comparison of model predictions with structural data

claim: The Piezo 1 force constant agrees with the Piezo 2 force constant within errors
source: which agrees with our results for Piezo 2 within errors (see Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Comparison of calculated values from simulation data

claim: In the flattened Piezo 1 structure, the distance between the residues L2469 of the three TM helices 38 is increased by 5 Å compared to the curved Piezo 1 structure
source: In the flattened Piezo 1 structure, the distance between the residues L2469 of the three TM helices 38 that line the ion channel is increased by 5 Å compared to the curved Piezo 1 structure, which indicates a widening of the outermost constriction site of the Piezo 1 ion channel formed by these residues (Yang et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to experimental work

claim: In coarse-grained simulations of membrane-embedded Piezo 1, a comparable widening of the ion channel is observed in response to tension-induced flattening
source: In our coarse-grained simulations of membrane-embedded Piezo 1, we observe a comparable widening of the ion channel lined by the three TM helices 38 in response to tension-induced flattening of the Piezo 1 protein.
evidence: Observed in simulation data

claim: The estimated change in excess area of 20 nm² is significantly smaller than previous estimates based on cryo-EM structures
source: which is significantly smaller than previous estimates based on cryo-EM structures, but still large compared to the area difference between the open and closed state of the ion channel
evidence: Comparison with literature estimates

claim: The estimated change in excess area is still large compared to the area difference between the open and closed state of the ion channel
source: but still large compared to the area difference between the open and closed state of the ion channel and, thus, in line with the suggested flattening-induced Piezo activation (Guo and MacKinnon, 2017).
evidence: Inference from comparison of calculated values

claim: The Piezo protein elasticity can be approximately described as a harmonic spring
source: According to this model, the Piezo protein elasticity can be approximately described as a harmonic spring, with a force-free conformation that agrees with the curved protein conformation in the cryo-EM structures within the modeling accuracy.
evidence: Derived from elasticity analysis of simulation data

claim: The force-free conformation of Piezo agrees with the curved protein conformation in the cryo-EM structures within the modeling accuracy
source: with a force-free conformation that agrees with the curved protein conformation in the cryo-EM structures within the modeling accuracy.
evidence: Derived from elasticity model and comparison with structural data

claim: With further tension-induced flattening, the force on the protein increases by about 60 pN per nanometer in reduced protein height
source: With further tension-induced flattening, the force on the protein increases by about 60 pN per nanometer in reduced protein height.
evidence: Calculated from elasticity model applied to simulation data

claim: Lin et al., 2019 measured the force-induced height change of Piezo1 protein-membrane nanodomes adsorbed to substrates using atomic force microscopy
source: With atomic force microscopy (AFM), Lin et al., 2019 measured the force-induced height change of Piezo1 protein-membrane nanodomes adsorbed to substrates.
evidence: Supported by citation to experimental work

claim: The smaller force response of about 7 pN per nanometer measured in AFM experiments cannot be compared to the force response of the protein obtained from modeling of simulation data
source: The smaller force response of about 7 pN per nanometer in reduced nanodome height measured in the AFM experiments, therefore, cannot be compared to the force response of the protein obtained from our modeling of simulation data for the tension-induced flattening of the Piezo protein-membrane nanodome.
evidence: Inference from differences in experimental systems

claim: In tensionless membranes, a nearly catenoidal shape of the membrane surrounding the Piezo protein nanodome is obtained in coarse-grained simulations
source: In tensionless membranes, we obtain a nearly catenoidal shape of the membrane surrounding the Piezo protein nanodome in our coarse-grained simulations, in agreement with calculations for radially symmetric nanodome shapes (Haselwandter and MacKinnon, 2018).
evidence: Observed in simulation data and consistent with theoretical calculations

claim: For tension values equal to or larger than 2.8 mN/m, the membrane profile is planar for radial distances larger than about 17 nm from the channel center
source: For tension values equal to or larger than 2.8 mN/m, in contrast, the membrane profile obtained from our coarse-grained simulations is planar for radial distances larger than about 17 nm from the channel center (see Figure 2d).
evidence: Observed in simulation data

claim: The results of coarse-grained simulations are independent of the finite membrane size in the simulations for tension values equal to or larger than 2.8 mN/m
source: The results of our coarse-grained simulations thus are independent of the finite membrane size in the simulations, at least for tension values equal to or larger than 2.8 mN/m.
evidence: Inferred from comparison of crossover length with simulation box size

claim: The simulation box area of about 33 × 33 nm² in atomistic simulations is larger than the simulation box area in previous atomistic simulations
source: The simulation box area of about 33 × 33 nm2 in our atomistic simulations is larger than the simulation box area in previous atomistic simulations (see Introduction)
evidence: Comparison with literature

claim: The simulation box area in atomistic simulations is clearly smaller than the corresponding area of about 50 × 50 nm² in coarse-grained simulations
source: but clearly smaller than the corresponding area of about 50 × 50 nm2 in our coarse-grained simulations.
evidence: Comparison of simulation parameters

claim: The trajectory lengths up to 300 ns of atomistic simulations are clearly shorter than the trajectory lengths between 4 and 8 μs of coarse-grained simulations
source: In addition, the trajectory lengths up to 300 ns of the computationally significantly more demanding atomistic simulations are clearly shorter than the trajectory lengths between 4 and 8 μs of our coarse-grained simulations.
evidence: Comparison of simulation parameters

claim: Limiting the excess area calculation up to radial distances 12 nm from the channel center leads to values that are only about 10% smaller than the values for the entire average shape
source: In the case of the tensionless average shapes obtained from our coarse-grained simulations, limiting the excess area calculation up to radial distances 12 nm from the channel center where the outermost 4-TM helix units are located (see Figure 1d) leads to values that are only about 10% smaller than the values for the entire average shape with maximal radial distance of about 25 nm.
evidence: Calculated from simulation data

claim: The smaller membrane area of atomistic simulations appears to be sufficient to capture the main deformations of the nanodome in tensionless membranes
source: The smaller membrane area of our atomistic simulations thus appears to be sufficient to capture the main deformations of the nanodome in tensionless membranes.
evidence: Inferred from analysis of excess area contributions

claim: The atomistic simulation trajectories start from a membrane shape obtained in coarse-grained simulations after 200 ns of relaxation
source: The atomistic simulation trajectories start from a membrane shape obtained in coarse-grained simulations after 200 ns of relaxation (see Materials and methods), which is converted to atomistic resolution.
evidence: Description of simulation protocol

claim: Within 200 ns of relaxation in coarse-grained simulations, the excess area of 165 nm² for the initial nanodome with cryo-EM Piezo 2 structure is reduced by about half
source: Within these 200 ns of relaxation in coarse-grained simulations, the excess area of 165 nm2 for the initial nanodome with cryo-EM Piezo 2 structure as starting structure is reduced by about half.
evidence: Observed in simulation data

claim: The initial relaxation in coarse-grained simulations facilitates the relaxation towards equilibrium in the atomistic simulations
source: The initial relaxation in coarse-grained simulations facilitates the relaxation towards equilibrium in the atomistic simulations.
evidence: Inference from simulation protocol design

claim: The Piezo 2 simulation system is based on the cryo-EM structure of the full-length Piezo 2 trimer (PDB ID 6KG7)
source: Our Piezo 2 simulation system is based on the cryo-EM structure of the full-length Piezo 2 trimer (PDB ID 6KG7; Wang et al., 2019), which includes all 38 TM helices of the Piezo 2 monomers.
evidence: Description of simulation setup

claim: Shorter loops of less than 25 residues not resolved in the cryo-EM structure were added with the software MODELLER v10.2
source: We added shorter loops of less than 25 residues not resolved in this cryo-EM structure with the software MODELLER v10.2 (Sali and Blundell, 1993; Webb and Sali, 2016).
evidence: Description of modeling procedure

claim: The unresolved 12 N-terminal TM helices were added to the Piezo 1 cryo-EM structure via homology modeling using the Piezo 2 structure as template
source: We therefore used the cryo-EM structure of full-length Piezo2 as template structure to add the unresolved 12 N-terminal TM helices to the Piezo 1 cryo-EM structure with PDB ID 6B3R (Guo and MacKinnon, 2017) via homology modeling with MODELLER v10.2.
evidence: Description of modeling procedure

claim: The Martini 2.2 force field was used in all coarse-grained simulations
source: We used the Martini 2.2 force field, which exhibits a general 4–1 mapping of non-hydrogen atoms into coarse-grained simulation beads (de Jong et al., 2013; Periole and Marrink, 2013; Marrink et al., 2007; Monticelli et al., 2008), in all coarse-grained simulations performed with the software GROMACS 2018.3 (Abraham et al., 2015).
evidence: Description of simulation methodology

claim: An asymmetric membrane composition was chosen that mimics the cell membrane composition with negatively charged lipids in the inner leaflet
source: As in previous simulation studies of membrane-embedded Piezo proteins (Buyan et al., 2020; Chong et al., 2021; De Vecchis et al., 2021; Jiang et al., 2021), we chose an asymmetric membrane composition that mimics the cell membrane composition with negatively charged lipids in the inner leaflet.
evidence: Description of simulation setup

claim: In atomistic simulations, the CHARMM36 force field was used
source: In our atomistic simulations, we used the CHARMM36 force field (Huang and MacKerell, 2013; Klauda et al., 2010) with the TIP3P water model (Jorgensen et al., 1983).
evidence: Description of simulation methodology
